newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lihir says on track for May 1997 start.
newsitem.headline: Lihir says on track for May 1997 start.

text.p: Lihir Gold Ltd said on Friday that the giant Lihir gold project in Papua New Guinea was on track to begin processing ore next month.
"The project is on schedule for processing oxide ore in May 1997 and sulphide ore by October 1997," Lihir chairman Ross Garnaut said in the company's 1996 annual report.
The report made no mention of PNG's recent political crisis which ended after last week's decision by Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan to step aside.
Garnaut said project costs had risen about 10 percent above the original A$673 million budget but the company was confident it had sufficent fund and borrowing sources to complete construction.
Lihir said the project expected to produce about 175,000 ounces of gold in 1997, more than 550,000 ounces in 1998 and then about 600,000 ounces a year for 15 years.
The company said there was the potential to increase resources through exploration within its 40-year exclusive mining lease on Lihir Island.
The project has proven and probable ore reserves of 104 million tonnes, averaging 4.37 grams of gold per tonne for 14.6 million ounces of contained gold.
Lihir said it expected to spend A$500,000 on exploration in 1997 and A$1 million a year thereafter.

Lihir is owned 22.9 percent by Southern Gold, which is itself owned 75 percent by RTZ-CRA Ltd and 25 percent by Vengold Inc. Niugini Mining Ltd owns 17.15 percent and the PNG government and landowners 17.5 percent.
